<p id="description">Kotdex is a Kotlin framework for Discord bots on top of JDA. Commands, components and events are declared with annotations, and live messages are written as Compose functions.</p>

## Modules

| Module | Contents |
|---|---|
| `kotdex-core` | `Client`, annotations, option mapping, guards, autocomplete, prefix commands, builders, coroutine helpers |
| `kotdex-compose` | Compose runtime for Components V2 messages that update themselves when state changes |
| `samples/bot` | A runnable bot using both modules |

Requires Java 17 or newer.

## Installation

Kotdex is published through JitPack. The Compose runtime is resolved from Google Maven.

```kotlin
repositories {
    mavenCentral()
    google()
    maven("https://jitpack.io")
}

dependencies {
    implementation("com.github.revolutionxk.kotdex:kotdex-core:<version>")
    implementation("com.github.revolutionxk.kotdex:kotdex-compose:<version>")
}
```

Bots using `kotdex-compose` also apply the Compose compiler plugin:

```kotlin
plugins {
    kotlin("jvm") version "2.4.21"
    kotlin("plugin.compose") version "2.4.21"
}
```

## Client

```kotlin
suspend fun main() {
    val client = Client {
        intents += GatewayIntent.MESSAGE_CONTENT
        prefix = "!"
        guilds += 123456789012345678L
    }

    client.scan("com.example.bot")
    client.login(System.getenv("DISCORD_TOKEN"))
}
```

`scan` registers every `@Discord` class in the given packages. Classes with constructor dependencies are registered with `client.register(instance)`. Application commands are registered after login; when `guilds` is set they go to those guilds instead of being global, which makes them available immediately during development.

## Commands

```kotlin
@Discord
class Moderation {
    @Slash("ban", "Ban a member", permissions = [Permission.BAN_MEMBERS], guildOnly = true)
    suspend fun ban(
        event: SlashCommandInteractionEvent,
        @Option("member", "Who to ban") member: Member,
        @Option("reason", "Why", maxLength = 200) reason: String?,
        @Option("days", "Messages to delete", min = 0.0, max = 7.0) days: Int = 0,
    ) {
        member.ban(days, TimeUnit.DAYS).reason(reason).await()
        event.reply("${member.effectiveName} was banned.").await()
    }
}
```

Option types come from the Kotlin parameter type: `String`, `Int`, `Long`, `Double`, `Boolean`, `User`, `Member`, `Role`, `IMentionable`, `Message.Attachment`, any `GuildChannel` type and enums, which become choices. Nullable parameters and parameters with a default value are optional.

Parameters without `@Option` are injected by type: the event, `Client`, `JDA`, `Guild`, `User`, `Member`, `MessageChannel` and `Message`. `Message` is the command message for prefix commands, the target of message context menus and the message a component belongs to. `Guild` and `Member` are missing outside guilds, so declare them nullable in handlers that also run in direct messages.

| Annotation | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `@Slash` | slash command |
| `@SlashGroup` | turns the class into `/name subcommand`; `root` nests it as `/root name subcommand` |
| `@Option` | command option, with `autocomplete`, `min`, `max`, `minLength`, `maxLength` |
| `@ContextMenu` | user or message context menu |
| `@ButtonComponent`, `@SelectMenuComponent`, `@ModalComponent` | component handlers; `id` is a regular expression matched against the whole custom id |
| `@SimpleCommand` | prefix command; arguments are parsed into the `@Option` parameters and a `List<String>` option takes the rest |
| `@On`, `@Once` | event listeners; the event type is the parameter type |
| `@Guarded` | runs `Guard`s before the handler, class guards first |

```kotlin
object Moderators : Guard {
    override suspend fun check(event: GenericEvent): Boolean =
        (event as? Interaction)?.member?.hasPermission(Permission.MODERATE_MEMBERS) == true
}

object Languages : Autocompleter {
    override suspend fun complete(event: CommandAutoCompleteInteractionEvent) =
        listOf("Kotlin", "Rust", "Swift").map { Command.Choice(it, it) }
}
```

Handlers can be `suspend`. `RestAction.await()`, `JDA.await<Event>()` and `IModalCallback.awaitModal(modal)` turn JDA callbacks into suspending calls.

## Compose

```kotlin
@Slash("counter", "A live counter")
suspend fun counter(event: SlashCommandInteractionEvent) {
    event.replyCompose(onlyFor = event.user) { Counter() }
}

@Composable
fun Counter() {
    var count by remember { mutableIntStateOf(0) }

    Container(accent = LocalTheme.current.primary) {
        Text("Count: **$count**")
        ActionRow {
            Button("+1") { count++ }
            Button("Reset", style = ButtonStyle.DANGER) { count = 0 }
        }
    }
}
```

Composables: `Container`, `Text`, `Section`, `Thumbnail`, `Separator`, `MediaGallery`, `MediaItem`, `ActionRow`, `Button`, `LinkButton`, `StringSelect` and `EntitySelect`. `remember`, `LaunchedEffect`, `DisposableEffect` and composition locals work as in any Compose application.

- `replyCompose` answers an interaction and `sendCompose` posts to a channel; both return a `ComposeView`.
- Button and select lambdas receive the interaction event. When a lambda does not answer the interaction itself, the click is acknowledged with the updated message. A lambda that is still running after 2.5 seconds has its click deferred, so open modals or reply before doing slow work.
- Lambdas run on the single thread shared by all views. Use `await()` instead of `complete()`, and move blocking work to another dispatcher with `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`.
- State changes outside clicks, such as timers in `LaunchedEffect`, are batched into at most one edit per second.
- A view expires 14 minutes after its last interaction: effects are cancelled and its components are disabled. `LocalView.current.close()` ends it earlier.
- `LocalTheme` provides the colors from `Theme`; `KotdexTheme` overrides them for a subtree.

## Example

```shell
DISCORD_TOKEN=... DISCORD_GUILD=... ./gradlew :samples:bot:run
```

## Development

```shell
./gradlew build
```

`build` runs the tests, the ktlint check through Spotless and the ABI check against `api/*.api`.

- `./gradlew spotlessApply` formats the sources.
- `./gradlew updateKotlinAbi` records an intentional change to the public API.
- `./gradlew dokkaGenerate` writes the API reference to `build/dokka/html`.
